project_context.title: Theory Mapping for Split-Complex Subspace Emulation Experiments
project_context.purpose: This document maps which theories or assumptions were supported, challenged, or partially validated by the experimental QPU results. It does not claim formal proof of new physics.

challenged_theories_or_assumptions.theory_or_assumption: Split-complex logic is only mathematical and not executable on physical quantum hardware.
challenged_theories_or_assumptions.experimental_evidence: Split-complex-inspired mappings were executed reproducibly on IBM superconducting hardware with high recovery fidelity.
challenged_theories_or_assumptions.what_is_not_yet_proven: This does not establish physical split-complex particles or nonstandard quantum mechanics.
challenged_theories_or_assumptions.apa7_reference: Khrennikov, A. (2003). Hyperbolic quantum mechanics. Advances in Applied Clifford Algebras, 13(1), 1–9.

challenged_theories_or_assumptions.theory_or_assumption: Useful contradiction-tolerant logic cannot run on NISQ hardware.
challenged_theories_or_assumptions.experimental_evidence: Belnap-style contradiction-tolerant logical structures were represented and recovered on real QPUs.
challenged_theories_or_assumptions.what_is_not_yet_proven: No large-scale computational advantage has yet been demonstrated.
challenged_theories_or_assumptions.apa7_reference: Belnap, N. D. (1977). A useful four-valued logic. In Modern uses of multiple-valued logic (pp. 8–37). Springer.

challenged_theories_or_assumptions.theory_or_assumption: Deep reversible circuits necessarily collapse rapidly on NISQ devices.
challenged_theories_or_assumptions.experimental_evidence: 97.8% fidelity remained at 100,000 programmed gate-pair depth.
challenged_theories_or_assumptions.what_is_not_yet_proven: Physical pulse depth and scheduled-duration immunity have not been established.
challenged_theories_or_assumptions.apa7_reference: Preskill, J. (2018). Quantum computing in the NISQ era and beyond. Quantum, 2, 79.

supported_or_partially_supported_theorie.experimental_evidence: The chronology-loop experiment stabilized into a mixed-state equilibrium rather than random collapse under causal-feedback conditions.
supported_or_partially_supported_theorie.what_is_not_yet_proven: No physical closed timelike curves or time travel were demonstrated.
supported_or_partially_supported_theorie.apa7_reference: Deutsch, D. (1991). Quantum mechanics near closed timelike lines. Physical Review D, 44(10), 3197–3217.

supported_or_partially_supported_theorie.experimental_evidence: Local damage and scrambling still allowed nonlocal recovery of the logical payload.
supported_or_partially_supported_theorie.what_is_not_yet_proven: No proof of AdS/CFT, spacetime emergence, or physical wormholes.
supported_or_partially_supported_theorie.apa7_reference: Pastawski, F., Yoshida, B., Harlow, D., & Preskill, J. (2015). Holographic quantum error-correcting codes: Toy models for the bulk/boundary correspondence. Journal of High Energy Physics, 2015(6), 149.

supported_or_partially_supported_theorie.experimental_evidence: Information behaved like recoverable subsystem-style encoding under corruption.
supported_or_partially_supported_theorie.what_is_not_yet_proven: Formal operator-algebra code-distance scaling has not yet been measured.
supported_or_partially_supported_theorie.apa7_reference: Kribs, D. W., Laflamme, R., Poulin, D., & Lesosky, M. (2005). Operator quantum error correction. Quantum Information & Computation, 6(4), 382–399.

supported_or_partially_supported_theorie.experimental_evidence: The mapped subspace showed unusually stable recovery under several noise and sabotage conditions.
supported_or_partially_supported_theorie.what_is_not_yet_proven: Controlled noise-channel characterization has not yet been completed.
supported_or_partially_supported_theorie.apa7_reference: Lidar, D. A., Chuang, I. L., & Whaley, K. B. (1998). Decoherence-free subspaces for quantum computation. Physical Review Letters, 81(12), 2594–2597.
